source: Public IYKYD recordings and their automatic transcripts. Summaries are paraphrases; excerpt captions are automatic.

episodes.focus: Trust, habits, and why conversation matters
episodes.summary: I start with trust: how familiar ways of thinking become difficult to question, and why communicating what we notice matters. Engineering is my starting point for asking how to move forward without losing sight of the consequences.

moments.label: Finding a way to communicate what we notice
How the brain simplifies what we know

episodes.title: We simply cannot stop talking
episodes.clipLabel: Finding a way to communicate what we notice

episodes.focus: Hope, stability, and confidence
episodes.summary: How do you build confidence when the rules around you feel unstable? I connect education, engineering, and the pressure to act normally, asking how people can gain room to try, learn, and change their circumstances.

moments.label: The foundations of confidence
Better technology can be simpler

episodes.title: We act so normally
episodes.clipLabel: Better technology can be simpler

episodes.focus: Making room to change your mind
episodes.summary: I use academic self-correction as a model for everyday life: revisiting an idea should be something we can welcome. The episode asks why identity, sunk effort, and trust make it so difficult to admit that a familiar approach is no longer working.

moments.label: An analogy for revising our own ideas
Why admitting an error is difficult

episodes.title: We don't speak up all the time
episodes.clipLabel: Why admitting an error is difficult

episodes.focus: Identity in an automated attention economy
episodes.summary: Identity grows from effort and experience, but it also grows from what we are shown. I move from the constructive side of identity to the ways curated feeds and automated recommendations can steer our choices without much deliberate reflection.

moments.label: Building an identity through effort
From curated identities to automated feeds

episodes.title: Identity as a function of effort
episodes.clipLabel: From curated identities to automated feeds

episodes.focus: An April Fools’ argument about authority
episodes.summary: An intentionally inverted opening argues that we should stop questioning powerful people. I then reveal the April Fools’ setup and examine how confidence, status, and familiar stories can become substitutes for evidence.

moments.label: The April Fools’ performance turns back on itself
Communicating inside a closed feedback loop

episodes.title: Eat your iron pyrite
episodes.clipLabel: The April Fools’ performance turns back on itself

episodes.focus: Authority, allegiance, and speaking up
episodes.summary: I compare the release of parental control with the much larger problem of questioning authority. The question is how trust becomes allegiance, and how people can explain what feels wrong without hitting a wall of inherited certainty.

moments.label: Questioning authority without losing the relationship
When allegiance becomes a wall

episodes.title: Mayday Mayday (Mayday)
episodes.clipLabel: When allegiance becomes a wall

episodes.focus: Protecting attention for what matters
episodes.summary: Focus is about more than finishing a task. I ask what our media, advertising, and everyday rewards train us to care about, and argue for attention that reaches local people, real relationships, and small consistent efforts.

moments.label: Attention in a buyer-beware world
What do we actually reward?

episodes.title: Basically we are not locked in
episodes.clipLabel: What do we actually reward?

episodes.focus: Reason, transparency, and room for uncertainty
episodes.summary: I explore how to stay grounded in evidence while remaining open to unfamiliar possibilities. Transparent systems, healthy skepticism, and flexible reasoning become ways to think about problems too large for any one person to fully grasp.

moments.label: Why systems should be understandable
Making room for flexible thinking

episodes.title: Rhyme or reason
episodes.clipLabel: Making room for flexible thinking

episodes.focus: Ambiguity and our information diet
episodes.summary: I connect uncertainty, the desire for safety, and the appeal of easy answers. The information-diet analogy asks whether we choose what we consume with any of the care we might bring to planning a meal.

moments.label: When ambiguity becomes a source of power
Do we plan what we consume?

episodes.title: In plain sight
episodes.clipLabel: Do we plan what we consume?

episodes.focus: The consequences of compelling stories
episodes.summary: Ghost stories become an analogy for the excitement and fear that persuasive ideas create, especially in technology. I ask how to enjoy possibility while paying attention to the time, trust, and choices those stories take from us.

moments.label: The technology sector as a storyteller
Following the consequences of a story

episodes.focus: Convenience, rural life, and sustainability
episodes.summary: Time away from the city makes me question the infrastructure and convenience I take for granted. I examine my own assumptions about rural places, the pressure to keep growing, and what allows a community to sustain itself.

moments.label: The skills that convenience lets us forget
The impulse to minimize every burden

episodes.title: So far so good
episodes.clipLabel: The impulse to minimize every burden

episodes.focus: Changing beyond what already works
episodes.summary: Mutation is my metaphor for breaking out of habits that adaptation alone cannot fix. I ask how people can change without dismissing everything they have learned, and what kind of trust and support makes that possible.

moments.label: Habit, adaptation, and the fear of change
Changing without throwing away your past

episodes.title: Mutants

episodes.focus: Taking the questions into conversation
episodes.summary: The early questions become interviews about media literacy, information overload, and choice. People describe curating their feeds, protecting their privacy, and finding trustworthy sources; I introduce the idea of an overlay that can help us reflect on a live exchange.

moments.label: The first media-literacy interviews
Wanting agency without endless decisions

episodes.title: What are you scared of?
episodes.clipLabel: Wanting agency without endless decisions

episodes.focus: A reminder to stay present
episodes.summary: Slouching becomes an analogy for taking the easiest position in a difficult conversation. I explore the possibility of a small haptic reminder, then ask people how curiosity, preparation, and reflecting someone’s words back can help them stay engaged.

moments.label: The idea of a tap on the shoulder
Curiosity as a listening practice

episodes.title: My back is in pain and I can’t stand it
episodes.clipLabel: Curiosity as a listening practice

episodes.focus: Why good solutions fail to travel
episodes.summary: I borrow transfer learning from robotics to ask why an approach that succeeds in one place can fail elsewhere. Conversations about careers, community, and role models return to the importance of context, access, teaching, and a realistic path into participation.

moments.label: A robot leaves the laboratory

episodes.title: Not everything is just love or war
episodes.clipLabel: A solution needs context and support

episodes.focus: Finding a way to speak and act
episodes.summary: What happens when something feels broken but there is no clear route to change it? Interviews explore vulnerability, collective action, institutional frustration, and the different roles of experience and evidence. I ask how useful knowledge can reach us when we actually need it.

moments.label: Remembering an idea when it matters
When complaints have no path into action

episodes.title: Ouch, that shit hurt
episodes.clipLabel: When complaints have no path into action

episodes.focus: Choosing an information diet
episodes.summary: I take the information-diet metaphor into a grocery store. Interviews explore convenience, limited choices, purposeful research, and staying connected to people, asking what actually leaves us informed or sustained.

episodes.focus: Who gets heard in a conversation?
episodes.summary: The first real-time prototype trial accompanies conversations about missed voices, interruptions, and getting someone’s attention. I explore whether a gentle signal and clearer group practices could help people participate without making the exchange feel policed.

episodes.summary: I bring a watch into the prototype setup and meet people speaking up about 3D-printing policy. The interviews connect privacy and open-source tools to personal motivation: what makes someone move from concern to showing up in person?

episodes.focus: Staying curious in a space full of choices
episodes.summary: A museum becomes a way to think about conversation: each person has more to explore than a quick exchange can hold. Visitors describe drawing, following what they love, and making a plan as ways to slow down and give their attention somewhere meaningful.

episodes.focus: How much can five words hold?
episodes.summary: I ask people to describe a difficult experience in about five words. Choosing those words becomes part of the conversation, revealing how much emotion and context a short response can carry. The live prototype runs alongside one of the exchanges.

episodes.focus: Making room for an unexpected answer
episodes.summary: A deliberately impatient opening gives way to short exchanges about interests, dislikes, work, and how people feel. The different answers explore how an open invitation can lead somewhere unexpected; the prototype’s transcript and feedback remain visible alongside the conversations.
